land.text: the Emishi domains of northern Honshu left after 802: Aomori, northern Iwate, most of Akita and Yamagata, under the Abe general who 'levied taxes and confiscated property on his own' in 1050

successors.note: The Emishi page gives no end for the Emishi as a political body; 1051 is the year the Abe, 'the general overseeing the Emishi', broke with the court (Former Nine Years' War). Dewa passed to the Kiyohara after 1062 (heian-japan dossier).

correction.text: the Emishi lands of the north-east: the Tohoku region without the part inside Cliopatria's Asuka Japan outline

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a people Cliopatria lacks. The Emishi page gives no boundary: it dates the first mention to 478 (Book of Song, '55 kingdoms' of the hairy people in the East) and the 658 voyage to Aguta (Akita). The land is the Tohoku region minus the court's Cliopatria shape (about 55,000 km2 by the gazetteer); the page has no area. Confidence in the extent is low.

correction.text: the same land without the Ideha foothold near Akita ('In 709, the fort of Ideha was created close to present day Akita')

keyframe_review.note: The court's Dewa foothold: Akita Castle page has Dewa created from northern Echigo in 708 and raised to a province in 712 'but the court still lacked effective control'.

correction.text: without the Akita foothold and the Sendai plain, where 'Taga Fort was built by Ōno no Omi Azumahito near present-day Sendai' in 724

keyframe_review.note: Taga Fort 724; the 737 road from Akita to Taga (Akita Castle page) joins the two footholds but gives no land.

correction.text: without the Akita foothold and Miyagi, where the army 'penetrated into what is now northern Miyagi Prefecture' and built Momonofu Castle in 758

keyframe_review.note: From 774 the Miyagi land and the Kitakami valley are the war zone (contest in the ledger); the shape is the Emishi land outside it. The Shiwa and Isawa Emishi hold the Kitakami valley and the north throughout.

correction.text: north of the Kitakami: after Aterui's surrender in 802 'North of the Kitakami River, the Emishi were still independent'; the court holds the Isawa land around Hiraizumi, Miyagi and the Akita foothold

keyframe_review.note: Mirrors the heian-japan dossier's 802-1061 shape (Heian 814 outline plus Hiraizumi 40 km and Akita 50 km). From about 850 the heian-japan dossier draws these domains as its vassal tint ('semi-autonomous feudal domains in the north'); this dossier keeps the shape unchanged. About 32,000 km2 by the gazetteer.

region.text: the Emishi lands of the north-east

ledger.note: 478: the Chinese Book of Song records '55 kingdoms' of the hairy people in the East; the Emishi page's first dated mention. The page gives no territory, so the north-east outside the Yamato outline is the researcher's reading (confidence 1). The Nihon Shoki first uses the word Emishi in 720.

region.text: the Ideha fort 'close to present day Akita'

ledger.note: 709: the court founds the fort of Ideha near Akita. 'In 709, the fort of Ideha was created close to present day Akita'; the Emishi of Akita then attacked the Japanese settlements. The Akita Castle page has Dewa created in 708 and raised to a province in 712.
724: Taga Fort rises on the Sendai plain. 'Taga Fort was built by Ōno no Omi Azumahito near present-day Sendai'; he then built forts across the plain and into Yamagata.

region.text: what is now northern Miyagi Prefecture, with Momonofu Castle on the Kitakami River

ledger.note: 758: Momonofu Castle on the Kitakami. Fujiwara no Asakari's army 'penetrated into what is now northern Miyagi Prefecture'; the Isawa Emishi attacked the castle.

region.text: the Sendai plain and the Kitakami valley forts

ledger.note: 774: the Thirty-Eight Years' War begins. 'On 5 September, 774 CE, the Emishi stormed Monou castle and the rebellion began'; the Emishi counterattacked on a broad front; in 780 they burned villages on the Sendai plain.

region.text: the war zone passes to the Heian court

ledger.note: 794: bookkeeping handoff: the court moves to Heian-kyo and the war goes on (nara-japan dossier ends the contest here; the fighting runs to 811).

region.text: the Isawa and Shiwa Emishi's war zone

ledger.note: 794: the war under the Heian court. 'In 794, many key Shiwa Emishi, including Isawa no kimi Anushiko ... became allies of the Japanese', isolating the Isawa; the new shogun Sakanoue no Tamuramaro then attacked the Isawa.

region.text: the Isawa Emishi's land in the Kitakami valley

ledger.note: 802: Aterui surrenders. The campaign 'eventually led to Aterui's surrender in 802'; the large-scale threat ended with the defeat of the Isawa. 'North of the Kitakami River, the Emishi were still independent.' Region follows the heian-japan dossier (Hiraizumi 40 km).

region.text: the Kitakami valley and Sendai plain

ledger.note: 811: the Thirty-Eight Years' War is over. 'it was not until 811 that the so-called Thirty-Eight Years' War was over' (the infobox says 774-812).

region.text: the Emishi domains of the north, under the Abe

ledger.note: 1051: the Abe, 'the general overseeing the Emishi', break with the court. 'In 1050, the general overseeing the Emishi was Abe no Yoritoki', who 'levied taxes and confiscated property on his own'; the war runs 1051-1062. From about 850 these domains were the heian-japan dossier's vassal tint (Emishi page: 'By the mid-9th century, most of the land held by the Emishi in Honshu had been conquered'; the remaining domains were 'semi-autonomous'). The Emishi page ends no polity in 1051; this is the sister dossiers' convention.

wars.name: Abe no Hirafu's northern expeditions
wars.outcome: No land change recorded: the 180-ship expedition reached Aguta (Akita), allied with the Aguta, Tsugaru and Watarishima Emishi and, on the Akita Castle page, set up a fortification on the Mogami River.
wars.note: The Emishi page: 'In 658, Abe no Hirafu's naval expedition of 180 ships reached Aguta'; it adds that this remained the furthest northern penetration of the imperial army until the 16th century. The Asuka dossier does not record 658.

wars.name: Thirty-Eight Years' War

zones.text: the Sendai plain and the Kitakami valley

wars.outcome: The Isawa Emishi under Aterui won at the Koromo River in 789 and surrendered in 802; the war was over in 811. Court gains: the Isawa land; the Emishi north of the Kitakami stayed independent.

wars.name: Former Nine Years' War
wars.outcome: Imperial victory at Kuriyagawa in 1062; Abe no Sadato surrendered. The Emishi domains pass to the court's governors.
wars.note: Listed because it ends the Emishi lands; the Abe are the belligerent, not the Emishi as a body.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the page names forts and rivers (Taga, Momonofu, the Kitakami), never a boundary; the Kitakami line after 802 is the page's own words.

notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from four pages (Emishi, Thirty-Eight Years' War, Akita Castle, Former Nine Years' War). Emishi is a people and a loose set of chiefdoms ('55 kingdoms'), typed state so that the Asuka, Nara and Heian gains have a counterpart. No capital, no rulers. Start 478 is the first dated mention (Book of Song), not a founding; the extent before 709 is the researcher's reading (Tohoku minus the Cliopatria Asuka outline). End 1051 follows the heian-japan dossier (vassal_end emishi 1051, Abe break); the Emishi page itself says most Emishi land was conquered by the mid-9th century and that the Abe and Kiyowara 'moved into Mutsu and Dewa perhaps during the 9th century', so a reviewer may prefer ending the Emishi c. 850 and treating 850-1051 as the Abe domain. Mirror events: 709, 724, 758, 774, 794, 802, 811 against asuka-japan, nara-japan, heian-japan. Not on the pages: the 878 Ganki (Gangyo) disturbance is only a name on the Akita Castle page ('Ganki Disturbance', destroyed much of the castle) and moved no border; Shiwa and Isawa Castle dates; any Emishi area figure (the infobox has none, so the area comparison is not applicable). Needs a dossier: abe-clan (written by this batch). No gazetteer names missing: Tohoku, Miyagi, Akita and Hiraizumi resolve.
